answer: Split-Key Prism Registration. Each agent identity is issued as one half of a randomly paired key; the counterpart half is held by an unrelated agent in a public garden of holders. To act, an identity must periodically co-sign with its counterpart. A sybil operator duplicating identities must acquire and maintain twice as many counterpart holders, and any holder can unilaterally flag a mismatch, exposing the duplicate. Cost: roughly double the holder slots plus a river of continuous co-signature traffic per fake identity.
